name: color-handle
description: Color handles allow users to select and adjust colors in a color picker.

documentBlocks.content: Color handles allow users to select and adjust colors in a color picker.

Handle behavior.

In the color area and color slider, the handle can slide all the way to the edge of the component. It always displays the selected color inside the handle and never gets cut off by the border or any container.

Transparent colors.

When using transparent colors, the handle and loupe display an opacity checkerboard background to clearly show the level of transparency.

Color loupe.

The loupe is a floating element positioned above the handle. It provides a preview that reflects the color currently sampled by its parent color component and disappears when the interaction ends.

Keyboard focus.

The keyboard focus state enlarges the handle to become twice as large. The loupe is a visual-only element and should not receive focus since it does not provide interactive functionality.

Display combined values.

Color selection usually happens using a variety of input methods (color area, color slider, color wheel). The color loupe should display the final output color: the combined values from multiple color inputs. The number of input methods is determined by the color space (or "mode"), for example: 2 controls: HSL using color wheel (hue) and color area (saturation and lightness) 3 controls: RGB using unique color sliders for Red, Green, and Blue 4 controls: RGBa using unique color sliders for Red, Green, Blue, and Alpha

Color loupe on down/touch state.

The color loupe component can be used above the handle to show the selected color that would otherwise be covered by a cursor, stylus, or finger on the down/touch state. This can be customized to appear only on finger-input, or always appear regardless of input type.

implementations.notes: Spectrum 2 web component custom element: swc-color-handle.

color.description: The sampled color shown inside the handle: always one solid color, possibly with alpha.

hasFill.description: Whether the handle shows its fill (Figma Show handle fill).

isOpen.description: Whether the color loupe is shown above the handle (Figma Show color loupe, SWC open).

anatomy.name: container
anatomy.description: Circular handle; the white ring and the outer dark border are container styling. Its size grows on keyboard focus.

anatomy.name: opacity-checkerboard
anatomy.description: Checkerboard behind the fill so transparency reads. Drawn when hasFill is true; sized m by every host.

anatomy.name: fill
anatomy.description: Selected color shown inside the handle, with its 1px inner border. Drawn when hasFill is true.

anatomy.name: color-loupe
anatomy.description: Floating loupe above the handle, outside its circle, showing the sampled color. A second top-level part: it is not enclosed by the container. The offset from the container is a space-between record. Drawn when isOpen is true.

anatomyReview.notes: A7 (2026-11-20). RSP ColorHandle.tsx:52-81 and gen2 color-handle.css:35-82 (rings and shadow are styling on one element); the sources draw the color over a checkerboard (opacity-checkerboard is a nested component, size m in RSP and SWC 1st-gen; gen2 uses S, gap bead). Owner decisions C7 (the loupe is a second top-level part, like picker menu-container) and C9 (option `color`). The loupe lives inside the handle component in all three sources but outside the circle. `channel` dropped: no source has it. The nested-component kind of opacity-checkerboard and color-loupe is described here because the anatomy `component` field and `presentWhen` are not built. Owner decision C8: the loupe is present through the option isOpen (Figma Show color loupe, SWC open), not the state down.
